sentence: Read the polyester composition details alongside the construction rather than treating the fiber name as the description of the whole garment.
en_before: Polyester and nylon are common synthetics. Viscose, modal and lyocell are regenerated cellulose fibers. Grouping everything as man-made can obscure construction and processing differences. Retaining exact fiber names is more useful than assuming all manufactured fibers are stuffy or easy-care.

sentence: Identify knitted fabric construction separately from fiber origin so visible stretch does not become a shortcut for guessing composition.
en_before: Poplin, twill and satin commonly describe woven constructions; jersey and rib commonly describe knits. If you cannot remember every term, ask simple questions: structured or draping, stretchy or not, lined or unlined, and what does the composition label say? Specific answers beat a long list of names.
